title: The Goal the Whole Team Scored
coreQuestion: How did Carlos Alberto's 1970 final goal come from a team-wide move?

facts.claim: Brazil beat Italy in the 1970 World Cup final, played at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.
The move is often regarded as one of the greatest team goals of all time.
Pelé drew the Italian defence into the centre and fed captain Carlos Alberto on the right flank for the final score.
Carlos Alberto captained Brazil to the 1970 World Cup and scored the fourth goal in the final, considered one of the greatest goals in the tournament's history.
The move began with Clodoaldo dribbling past Italian players in his own half.
Jairzinho passed to Pelé, who rolled the ball into the path of Carlos Alberto.
Carlos Alberto struck the ball into the net with a powerful shot.

narration.text: One goal, often called the greatest team goal ever.
The 1970 World Cup final. Brazil against Italy, at the Azteca.
The move ran through the team.
Pelé drew the Italian defence into the middle, and fed him on the right.
Carlos Alberto scored the fourth goal. Every goal has a story.
